data.name: v8.4.216 - `ultralytics 8.4.216` ST Edge AI export for STM32 devices (#27291)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.216 adds export support for STM32 edge devices and improves training, inference reliability, and deployment guidance across the ecosystem.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- **STM32 export with ST Edge AI:** The new `format="stedgeai"` export creates ONNX models for ST Edge AI Core and STM32 devices, including STM32N6. It supports float and INT8 export, with normalized detection and keypoint coordinates to support whole-graph quantization. This is the release’s main feature and also enables Ultralytics Platform to offer the format.
- **Better training behavior on AMD GPUs:** ROCm training now keeps the NCHW layout by default, avoiding a layout that was substantially slower on some Radeon hardware. AMD GPU metrics are also reported during ROCm training.
- **More reliable model use and exports:** Fixes include support for YOLOE prompts and TorchScript with PyTorch 2.16, correct CPU handling for `device="cpu:0"`, and restored top-1 accuracy for INT8 LiteRT and NXP classification exports.
- **Fixes for validation, masks, and video:** Validation now keeps separate per-image metrics for same-named files in different folders and handles mixed relative and absolute paths. Segmentation masks remain correct when results are converted to another dtype, and saved video duration is preserved when the effective frame rate is below 1 FPS.
- **More robust image and solution handling:** Local HEIC and AVIF images are supported in LLM requests; several image-reading paths now respect photo orientation. Heatmaps and tracking zones also handle changes in frame size more reliably.
- **Expanded practical guidance:** The preprocessing guide now includes a runnable dataset audit and advice for addressing class imbalance. The model-configuration guide explains how to start a YOLO26 P2 model from standard pretrained weights, with the trade-off that the extra small-object output increases computation.
- **Updated deployment documentation and examples:** Several integration guides—including Core ML, LiteRT, NCNN, RKNN, Ascend, and DEEPX—were reorganized with clearer export requirements, output details, and limitations. Python examples were consolidated into shared ONNX Runtime and OpenCV DNN examples covering multiple tasks.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Bring YOLO to smaller, low-power hardware:** STM32 users gain a direct export path for compiling models with ST’s tools, including an INT8 option suited to constrained devices.
- **Avoid slow or incorrect workflows:** ROCm layout changes improve training performance on affected GPUs, while the bug fixes reduce errors and preserve outputs across validation, inference, and export.
- **Make deployment easier to plan:** Clearer integration guides help users choose settings, understand exported outputs, and spot hardware or version requirements before deployment.
- **Help users catch dataset issues earlier:** The audit makes it easier to find class imbalance, validation-only classes, and duplicate images before spending time on training.

data.name: v8.4.215 - `ultralytics 8.4.215` Plot, convert and prompt segmentation masks without the dense mask stack (#27216)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**YOLO 8.4.215 improves segmentation memory efficiency and fixes several data, tracking, and reliability issues—without changing model architectures or default prediction settings.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🧠 **Lower-memory segmentation workflows (main release change):** Plotting, saving, displaying, moving, and prompting segmentation masks can now work with masks stored inside their bounding boxes instead of building a full image-sized mask stack. Outputs and defaults remain unchanged; requesting `masks.data` still creates the dense masks.
- 🏷️ **More reliable automatic annotations:** Class labels stay matched to their detections when SAM filters out some masks.
- 🎥 **More complete video predictions:** Video loading now reads frames until decoding ends, rather than stopping at a possibly inaccurate frame count in the file metadata.
- 🧭 **More dependable tracking fallback:** If ECC camera-motion estimation fails, the tracker now retains the identity transform instead of potentially using a partially modified estimate.
- 📌 **Accurate checkpoint provenance:** Checkpoints record the Git commit present when the run starts, even if the checkout changes later.
- 🧠 **Updated Brain Tumor dataset:** Now contains 1,115 brain MRI images, one `tumor` class, and a patient-based validation split. Documentation clarifies that it is for research and education, not clinical diagnosis.
- 🛠️ **Improved CI resilience and documentation:** CI retries a failed asset-cache restore once, and several documentation page titles are clearer and more distinct.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🚀 Segmentation workflows can avoid the memory and processing cost of a dense stack when they only need masks within detected boxes. This can help with larger images or many detections while preserving existing outputs.
- ✅ Annotation, video, and tracking fixes reduce the chance of incorrect labels, silently skipped frames, or unreliable camera-motion compensation.
- 🔍 Checkpoint metadata makes it easier to identify the exact code used for a training run.
- 📚 The revised dataset split and guidance make the Brain Tumor dataset easier to use appropriately, while its limitations remain important: it has no tumor-free examples and is not suitable for clinical diagnosis.
- 🔧 No new model architecture or change to prediction defaults is introduced in this release.

## What's Changed
* Record the launch commit in checkpoint git metadata by @fcakyon in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27213
* Fix ECC identity fallback after failed motion estimation by @AhmetMert01 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27219
* Give the settings docs page a distinct title by @miles-deans-ultralytics in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26595
* Keep auto-annotation classes aligned when SAM drops masks by @aswanth-07 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27214
* Shorten front-matter titles on 25 docs pages by @miles-deans-ultralytics in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26316
* Read video frames until capture ends by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27215
* fix: retry failed CI asset restores once by @fcakyon in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27220
* Update brain-tumor dataset to one tumor class with a patient-id validation split by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27218
* `ultralytics 8.4.215` Plot, convert and prompt segmentation masks without the dense mask stack by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27216


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.214...v8.4.215

data.name: v8.4.214 - Read every image upright: apply EXIF orientation for all formats and flags (#27168)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.214 makes image orientation consistent across reads**, helping ensure labels, predictions, and displayed images all use the same upright view. It also includes platform, hardware-compatibility, and reliability fixes, plus a substantially refreshed OpenVINO guide.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🖼️ **EXIF orientation is now applied consistently when reading images**, across supported formats, read flags, and OpenCV versions. This is the release’s main functional change: images should appear in the same orientation that viewers display, reducing the risk of labels or predictions being rotated relative to the image.
- 📚 **OpenVINO documentation was reorganized and expanded** with clearer export and deployment steps, INT8 quantization guidance, device behavior and limitations, and updated benchmarks for YOLO26 on server CPUs and Intel Core Ultra hardware. The guide documents deployment options rather than introducing a new model.
- 🧠 **Segmentation mask shape checks avoid building full mask arrays** when only the shape is requested, reducing unnecessary memory use.
- 🖥️ **GPU detection now uses PyTorch’s device list**, allowing AMD GPUs to be detected even when NVIDIA tools such as `nvidia-smi` or NVML are unavailable. Idle-GPU checks are skipped when utilization data cannot be read.
- 🧰 **Several edge cases were fixed:** thin images no longer resize to zero pixels during compression; Windows can download weights from HTTP(S) URLs; and bounding-box-to-segmentation conversion keeps labels separate for matching image names in different subfolders.
- 🧹 **RT-DETR training no longer reports unused class weights.** This cleans up logging; training losses are unchanged.
- 📝 **Platform and usage docs were updated** to explain the 1,000-prediction limit for most Platform YOLO workflows (300 for RT-DETR), image rotation controls, cloud-training project naming, and prediction examples.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ **More reliable image handling:** applying EXIF orientation consistently helps prevent annotation and inference mismatches, especially for images with embedded rotation metadata.
- ⚡ **Less unnecessary memory work:** querying segmentation mask dimensions no longer expands box-local masks into full-image masks.
- 🌐 **Broader hardware and platform support:** AMD GPU detection and Windows URL downloads work more reliably, while the documentation better explains how to deploy YOLO26 with OpenVINO.
- 🛠️ **Safer data workflows:** compression and label conversion now handle thin images and nested train/validation directories without the associated failures or overwritten labels.

## What's Changed
* Platform docs: 1,000 detections per image, local save directory project naming, cloud training title by @pderrenger in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27204
* Update YouTube video link in `predict` docs by @RizwanMunawar in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27205
* Fix zero-sized dimensions in image compression by @AhmetMert01 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27201
* Download URL weights on Windows in `attempt_download_asset` by @MohammadHijjawi97 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27202
* Keep train and val labels separate in yolo_bbox2segment by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27209
* Read segmentation mask shapes without building the full mask stack by @aswanth-07 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27207
* Restructure the OpenVINO integration page and add server CPU benchmarks by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27208
* Detect AMD GPUs when nvidia-smi and NVML are unavailable by @AIwork4me in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27203
* Stop RT-DETR training from logging unused cls_pw class weights by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27210
* Read every image upright: apply EXIF orientation for all formats and flags by @sergiuwaxmann in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27168

## New Contributors

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.213...v8.4.214

data.name: v8.4.213 - `ultralytics 8.4.213` Decode large segmentation mask stacks inside their boxes (#27197)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.213 makes large segmentation predictions more memory- and compute-efficient, while also improving data handling, inference reliability, and deployment documentation.** 🚀

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Faster handling of large segmentation masks (PR #27197):** For large mask stacks, prediction now decodes each mask within its detection box rather than across the whole image. Outlines and exports can use these box-local masks directly; the familiar dense `masks.data` tensor is created only when requested. Smaller mask stacks keep the existing path.
- **More reliable tiled predictions:** Tile-seam detections are no longer suppressed by overlapping detections from a different class when class-aware NMS is enabled.
- **Safer dataset conversion:** COCO conversion now errors instead of mixing labels when different images map to the same label file. SAM-based segmentation conversion also keeps class IDs matched to the masks that survive filtering.
- **Improved results and visualization:** Fixes correct confusion-matrix percentages for datasets with over 100 classes, and correct red/blue color handling for PIL images and SAM3 tensor results.
- **Platform and OCR improvements:** Training can upload initial batch previews to the Platform; local run paths produce cleaner Platform project names. OCR now shares the ONNX Runtime setup used by YOLO models.
- **Clearer guidance:** ONNX and TensorRT documentation was reorganized and expanded with output formats, deployment details, and refreshed benchmarks. Validation export docs now describe per-class metrics.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Segmentation users with many detections or large images** may see lower mask-processing costs, especially when they need outlines or exports but do not read the full mask tensor. Accessing `masks.data` still produces the usual dense result.
- **Tiled detection users** are less likely to lose valid objects at tile boundaries just because an overlapping object belongs to another class.
- **Dataset creators and evaluators** get clearer failures for conflicting label paths and more trustworthy class metrics.
- **Deployers and Platform users** benefit from clearer export guidance, more consistent OCR runtime behavior, and more useful training previews. No model architecture change is included in this release.

## What's Changed
* Show correct confusion matrix percentages on Platform for models with over 100 classes by @laodouya in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27183
* Keep tiled detections that overlap an object of a different class by @AhmetMert01 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27188
* OCR uses the same ONNX Runtime setup as YOLO models by @Laughing-q in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27189

* Fix swapped red and blue in Annotator PIL images and SAM3 tensor results by @AhmetMert01 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27196
* Add epoch-0 training visual uploads by @Laughing-q in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27173

data.name: v8.4.212 - `ultralytics 8.4.212` Read Korean, Cyrillic, Arabic and other scripts with OCR (#27167)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.212 expands OCR to more writing systems and improves Platform discovery, data import, training reliability, and inference compatibility.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🌍 **OCR supports more languages and scripts.** Choose a PP-OCRv5 model to recognize Korean, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai, Greek, Tamil, or Telugu text. These models run through ONNX Runtime, without requiring PaddlePaddle or PaddleOCR. For example:
  ```python
  ocr = solutions.OCR(recognizer="korean_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec")
  result = ocr(im0)
  ```
  Select the model for the text you expect; OCR does not automatically identify or switch languages. Hebrew is not included in the new models.
- 🔎 **Platform Explore adds a Models tab.** Search public models by what they detect, browse results, and try or clone models. The Platform docs also cover direct imports from hosted Label Studio, including supported detection, oriented-box, segmentation, and classification projects.
- 🧰 **Training and evaluation are more dependable.** Fixes prevent distributed training from hanging when canceled, restore deterministic training for certain tasks on older macOS MPS setups, and include mask, pose, and semantic pixel-accuracy details in exported validation summaries.
- ⚡ **Inference and export fixes improve compatibility and efficiency.** ONNX Runtime is better matched to CUDA 12 PyTorch installs and uses more suitable CPU thread limits; TensorRT checks recognize installations in NVIDIA containers and JetPack. MNN inputs, YOLOE tracking with ReID, and Edge TPU pose keypoints also receive fixes.
- 🛡️ **Data handling is safer and more efficient.** Detection crop saving avoids unnecessary full-image copies; segmentation-mask conversion now rejects filename collisions before overwriting labels; source lists consistently use UTF-8.
- 📚 **Documentation is refreshed.** Guides reflect current Platform features, and outdated DeepSparse documentation is removed because the project has reached end of life.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- People working with multilingual images can use a suitable OCR recognizer for scripts that the default PP-OCRv6 model does not cover.
- Platform users can more easily find relevant public models and bring supported hosted Label Studio projects into their workflow.
- Training, validation exports, and deployment should behave more reliably across distributed setups and a wider range of hardware and software versions.
- Safer file handling and reduced image copying help prevent accidental data loss and avoid unnecessary work.

## What's Changed

data.name: v8.4.211 - Encode images up to 9% faster with compiled SAM 3 (#27158)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.211 speeds up compiled SAM image encoding and expands model deployment options, with additional gains and fixes across training, OCR, and exports.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🚀 **Faster compiled SAM 3 and SAM 3.1:** The image encoders run **7–9% faster** in the tested `torch.compile` setup. The optimization is specific to compiled execution; eager-mode results remain unchanged.
- 📦 **Static INT8 export for ExecuTorch:** Models can now be exported in a smaller INT8 format with calibration data. Detection, segmentation, pose, and oriented-box heads remain in FP32 to help preserve prediction quality.
- 📝 **Faster OCR on NVIDIA GPUs:** OCR can use a cached FP16 TensorRT engine, which the release reports is about **2.5× faster than ONNX Runtime on dense pages** after its initial engine build. The OCR guide also clarifies which writing systems the default recognizer supports.
- ⚡ **Faster deterministic training:** Semantic segmentation and depth workloads use a faster resizing path when deterministic mode is enabled; measured speedups reached **3.9×** for one semantic segmentation setup.
- ⚖️ **Class weighting for classification:** The `cls_pw` training option now accounts for class imbalance in classification datasets, as well as detection.
- 🖥️ **Faster CPU pooling:** SPPF uses an equivalent pooling approach on CPU, reducing measured block latency by **22–45%** without changing GPU or exported-model behavior.
- 🛠️ **Export and input fixes:** TensorRT INT8 keeps additional sensitive head layers in floating point; legacy CoreML INT8 exports are fixed; and fixes address Tiger-Pose keypoint flips and classification on float NumPy inputs.
- 📚 **Platform and documentation updates:** Guides now cover items such as PDF prediction uploads, crowded prediction results, stopped-deployment metrics, dataset cloning limits, and PP-OCRv6 language coverage.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Compiled SAM users can process images faster without changing the eager-mode path.
- ExecuTorch users gain a smaller deployment option, while keeping important prediction heads at higher precision.
- OCR users on NVIDIA GPUs can reduce recognition time on dense pages, while users of unsupported scripts are less likely to mistake detections for accurate text recognition.
- Training and CPU inference improvements can reduce run time for relevant workloads; actual gains depend on the device, model, and settings.
- Export and input fixes improve reliability when preparing models for TensorRT, CoreML, and other deployment workflows.

data.name: v8.4.210 - ultralytics 8.4.210 Use PyTorch device names for OpenVINO and LiteRT Intel CPU, GPU and NPU (#27136)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Release `v8.4.210` makes hardware selection more consistent across model formats, improves OCR for rotated text, and fixes several deployment and inference issues.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **One device naming convention — the main change:** OpenVINO and LiteRT now accept PyTorch-style device names. Use `cpu` for Intel CPU, `xpu` for Intel GPU, and `npu` for an Intel NPU with those runtimes. The `intel:cpu`, `intel:gpu`, and `intel:npu` names still work as deprecated aliases, with a warning. Device names are consistent, but their hardware mapping depends on the runtime—for example, PyTorch `npu` refers to Ascend, while OpenVINO and LiteRT use Intel NPU.
- **More capable OCR:** The OCR solution now uses PP-OCRv6 through ONNX Runtime, with YOLO26x-Text as its default detector. It can handle pages rotated sideways or upside down, group words into lines, and return them in reading order, without requiring PaddlePaddle. The optimized recognizer requires Python 3.11+ and ONNX Runtime 1.26+.
- **More reliable INT8 exports:** LiteRT and NXP exports keep detection, segmentation, pose, and OBB head outputs in FP32 while quantizing much of the rest of the model. This helps preserve confidence scores and box precision. For TensorRT INT8, RT-DETR’s transformer components are kept out of INT8 to avoid severe accuracy drops on TensorRT 11.3 and 11.4.
- **Inference and profiling fixes:** Float64 NumPy and tensor inputs are converted safely for Apple MPS, which does not support float64. ONNX model profiling also preserves fixed input dimensions when other dimensions are dynamic.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Simpler cross-format workflows:** The same device spelling can be used for prediction, validation, and benchmarking, with each runtime mapping it to its supported hardware. OpenVINO’s explicit `cpu` selection also now reliably means CPU rather than automatic device selection.
- **OCR that works on more real-world images:** Rotated documents and screenshots can be read and returned in a more useful reading order, with fewer extra framework dependencies.
- **Better quantized-model usability:** Users can benefit from smaller or faster INT8 deployments while avoiding key accuracy problems in model outputs and RT-DETR TensorRT engines.
- **Fewer device-specific surprises:** Float64 inputs are handled more consistently on MPS, and profiling is more compatible with ONNX models that have a mix of fixed and dynamic dimensions.

## What's Changed
* Read OCR text at any rotation with PP-OCRv6 on ONNX Runtime and benchmark-chosen YOLO26x-Text defaults by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27141
* Keep RT-DETR's AIFI and decoder out of INT8 so TensorRT 11.3 and 11.4 engines work by @atakann in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27122
* Keep LiteRT INT8 head outputs in float by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27053
* Preserve fixed ONNX input dimensions in model profiling by @aswanth-07 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27130
* Fix float64 NumPy and tensor predictions on MPS by @sohailshk in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27138
* Keep PP-OCRv6 character probabilities on the GPU in TextRecognizer by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27142
* Use PyTorch device names for OpenVINO and LiteRT Intel CPU, GPU and NPU by @onuralpszr in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27136

data.name: v8.4.209 - Correct results for every request when serving YOLO to many users at once (#27140)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.209 makes concurrent YOLO predictions more reliable and includes targeted fixes for validation, exports, and device-specific inference.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Correct results for concurrent requests:** Each prediction now applies its own settings—such as confidence threshold, IoU threshold, and image size—while holding the predictor’s inference lock. This prevents one request from accidentally using another request’s settings. The shared predictor still processes calls one at a time, so this improves correctness rather than parallel throughput.
- **More accurate validation filtering:** `val(classes=[...])` now filters predictions as well as ground-truth labels, so excluded classes are less likely to affect metrics or saved results.
- **Safer NCNN exports:** NCNN does not support a batch axis. Requests to export with `batch > 1` are now rejected before conversion, rather than potentially producing a model that crashes during prediction.
- **Fixes for specific hardware and precision cases:** Updates address mask-IoU accuracy under mixed precision, ONNX Runtime thread usage, ONNX inference on Apple MPS, Core AI export on Apple silicon, and OpenVINO exports and benchmarks on Intel devices. Intel NPU INT8 exports also use a quantization setting intended to improve performance on supported models.
- **Improved training and semantic-mask reliability:** Fixes prevent large Platform training-completion requests from being rejected and preserve class IDs in certain palette-based semantic masks.
- **Updated documentation and CI:** Platform guidance and pricing pages were refreshed, DOTA licensing guidance was clarified, and GPU CI now reuses cached assets to reduce unnecessary downloads.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **For teams serving many users:** Shared-model prediction results are more dependable when requests use different settings, reducing the risk of returning incorrect detections.
- **For model evaluation and deployment:** Class-filtered validation better reflects the requested classes, while unsupported NCNN batch settings fail early with a clear error.
- **For hardware users:** Targeted backend fixes can prevent crashes, incorrect results, or slowdowns on affected Apple, Intel, and ONNX Runtime setups.
- **For Platform and CI users:** Training completion is more resilient for large-class datasets, and GPU CI is less dependent on repeated downloads from GitHub Releases.

data.name: v8.4.208 - `ultralytics 8.4.208` Release the 0.5 predict NMS IoU default (#27102)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Ultralytics **8.4.208** ships practical inference, visualization, and performance updates—most notably a **0.5 default NMS IoU for prediction and tracking**, while validation keeps its 0.7 default.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🎯 **More selective prediction and tracking:** When `iou` is not specified, prediction and tracking now use `0.5` instead of `0.7`. Validation remains at `0.7`, and explicitly provided values still take precedence.
- 🖼️ **Better YOLOE visual-prompt results:** Calls using visual prompts now default to `conf=0.05`, helping retain more similar objects whose confidence scores may be low. Other prediction calls are unchanged.
- 🎨 **Custom class colors:** Class colors can be supplied with dataset metadata and carried through trained or exported models into prediction visualizations.
- ⚡ **Performance improvements:** Multi-GPU training with gradient accumulation avoids unnecessary gradient synchronization on batches that do not update the optimizer. NMS-free TensorRT 11 FP16 exports can also be up to 3% faster.
- 🌍 **Italian documentation access:** Italian links were added to documentation, README, and example notebook language bars.
- 📦 **Release:** Version 8.4.208 publishes these changes; it does not introduce a new model architecture.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Prediction and tracking should generally show fewer duplicate overlapping boxes by default. In crowded scenes, some nearby objects may also be suppressed, so users can adjust `iou` when needed.
- Lowering the visual-prompt confidence threshold can make “find similar objects” workflows more complete, though it may include weaker detections.
- Custom colors make classes easier to distinguish and keep annotation colors consistent across supported visualizations.
- Training and TensorRT speedups can reduce runtime for the affected multi-GPU and export workflows.

data.name: v8.4.206 - `ultralytics 8.4.206` Read upside-down and bottom-to-top text in OCR (#27083)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.206 improves PaddleOCR’s handling of upside-down text and makes OCR/rotated-box labels easier to read.** 🔄

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Reads upside-down text with PaddleOCR:** The OCR solution now uses a text-line orientation classifier to identify text that may be upside down. It tries those crops in both orientations and keeps the reading with higher confidence. This also helps with bottom-to-top text when its crop is oriented upside down.
- **Updates OCR dependencies:** PaddleOCR now requires `paddleocr>=3.7` and PaddlePaddle 3.1 or later. Custom recognizers are unchanged and do not get automatic orientation correction.
- **Improves label placement:** OCR and oriented bounding-box labels now sit above the top-left of the box enclosing the polygon, rather than covering rotated text or appearing at an arbitrary corner. OCR labels also use black text on green for contrast.
- **Refreshes CI runner labels:** GitHub Actions now uses `macos-latest` and `ubuntu-26.04-arm` labels, reducing future maintenance as runner images change.
- **Clarifies NXP documentation:** The guide describes NXP’s Neutron SDK source as a pip package index instead of linking to a page that returns an error in browsers. Export behavior is unchanged.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **More reliable OCR:** PaddleOCR users should get better results on text that appears upside down, with the more confident reading selected automatically.
- **Clearer visualizations:** Labels are less likely to obscure text or polygons, making plotted results easier to inspect.
- **No change for custom OCR backends:** Users supplying their own recognizer remain responsible for handling text orientation.
- **No change to NXP exports:** The documentation link was corrected; pip-based SDK installation continues to work.

data.name: v8.4.205 - `ultralytics 8.4.205` Add scene text OCR solution with YOLO26-Text and PaddleOCR (#27061)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Release **8.4.205** adds a ready-to-use scene-text OCR solution, led by YOLO26-Text detection paired with PaddleOCR or a custom recognizer, alongside important tiled-inference and export fixes.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 📝 **New OCR solution:** Detects text with detection, OBB, or segmentation models, then recognizes it with optional PaddleOCR or a custom callable. Results include recognized text, confidence scores, original-image polygons, detection indices, and reading-order sorting. The core `Results` API remains unchanged.
- 🔤 **YOLO26-Text resources:** Adds guidance for the YOLO26-Text checkpoint family and a new OBB training dataset combining COCO-Text and HierText, with **65,325 images and about 1.29 million word polygons**.
- 🧩 **More reliable tiled inference:** Removes covered seam fragments, handles empty tiled predictions on Apple MPS, and fixes related segmentation, validation-memory, and class-count issues.
- 📦 **More dependable exports:** LiteRT and NXP exports now run on CPU to avoid failures on MPS and incorrect results on CUDA. DEEPX support is updated for DX-COM 2.5.0 and its matching runtime requirements.
- 📱 **Expanded deployment guidance:** Adds a MediaTek Dimensity Android guide and improves documentation for high-resolution tiling and DEEPX deployment.
- ✅ **Small correctness fixes:** `yolo checks` now ignores requirements that do not apply to the current environment, and dataset split fractions reject booleans instead of treating them as numbers.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- OCR users can build a text-reading workflow from detection through recognition without writing their own crop, ordering, and result-handling pipeline. PaddleOCR remains optional; custom recognizers can be plugged in.
- The new scene-text dataset makes it easier to train word detectors for signs, documents, receipts, and other real-world text. It provides detection annotations, not transcripts for recognition training.
- Tiled predictions should contain fewer duplicate or incomplete boxes at window seams, while fixes improve reliability for tiled segmentation and validation.
- CPU-based LiteRT and NXP export avoids device-specific export problems; DEEPX users should match DX-COM 2.5.0 models with **DX-RT 3.5.0 or newer**.
- The MediaTek guide clarifies that released Android support covers CPU and GPU inference; its NPU results use a prototype and are not yet supported by the released plugin.

data.name: v8.4.204 - Release 8.4.204 with High Resolution Tiling documentation (#27069)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Ultralytics **8.4.204** makes high-resolution tiling available across training, validation, and prediction, and adds improvements to FastSAM prompts, model exports, and dataset handling.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🧩 **High-resolution tiling:** Use `tile=True` or a positive integer tile size to process large images in overlapping windows. Training crops labels to each tile; validation and prediction merge results back into the original image.
- 📚 **Updated tiling documentation and examples:** A new **High Resolution Tiling** guide covers usage, supported tasks, and performance considerations. The SAHI guide remains available with a deprecation notice directing users to the built-in `tile` option, and the video example now uses the standard YOLO CLI and Python API.
- 🎯 **Better FastSAM text prompts:** FastSAM now uses a DataComp-XL CLIP model that selects the correct mask more often, with similar speed and download size.
- ⚡ **Faster LiteRT quantization:** INT8 and w8a16 calibration now use a C++ profiling mode. In the reported benchmark, export time dropped from about 36 seconds to 11 seconds, with no measured validation accuracy regression.
- 🛠️ **More dependable exports and calibration:** INT8 calibration now supports NDJSON and Platform datasets. NCNN export reports models its runtime cannot load, and dependency fixes address issues affecting TensorFlow, RKNN, Axelera, and Xilinx exports.
- 🔧 **Additional fixes:** RT-DETR INT8 export avoids known failures on certain SM 12.1 GPUs; resumed training uses new augmentation randomness; and the YAML parser accepts spaces before the colon after quoted keys.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🐜 Tiling can preserve small-object detail in large images without requiring a separate tiling package. It works across several vision tasks, but increases the number of model passes and may take more time and memory.
- 🚀 Export and calibration changes can make deployment workflows faster or more reliable, particularly on affected hardware and formats.
- 📖 Users can use the built-in tiling option throughout training, evaluation, and prediction, while the existing SAHI guide remains accessible with a deprecation notice.
- 📦 The release updates the package version to **8.4.204**. The release PR primarily updates documentation and examples; the other merged PRs provide the additional runtime and export changes.

## What's Changed
* Keep RT-DETR INT8 squeeze convs and attention in float on SM 12.1 (GB10, N1X) by @atakann in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27049
* Use profiler-based calibration for faster LiteRT INT8 and w8a16 export by @amanharshx in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27062
* Accept spaces before the colon after quoted YAML keys by @MohammadHijjawi97 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27052
* Fail NCNN export when NCNN cannot load the converted model by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27056

data.name: v8.4.203 - Add NXP i.MX95 Neutron export (#27047)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.203** adds NXP i.MX95 Neutron NPU export for YOLO models, plus security improvements and fixes across training, inference, tracking, and visualization.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🚀 **NXP i.MX95 export:** Export with `format=nxp` to create an INT8 LiteRT model compiled using Neutron SDK 3.3.0. The export supports all seven YOLO tasks and uses the existing LiteRT inference backend with NXP’s delegate. It targets **i.MX95 only**; unsupported operations may run on the CPU.
- 🔒 **Safer loading:** Dataset caches now use a restricted unpickler. Checkpoints no longer trigger automatic package installation, and SAM, NAS, YOLO-World, and YOLOE loading paths use safer weights-only loading where supported.
- 🧠 **Training fixes:** YOLOE text-prompt training now handles smaller class counts correctly, hand-keypoint flips preserve landmark assignments, and deterministic semantic-segmentation loss computation is faster.
- 🎯 **Inference and tracking fixes:** Tracker assignment now finds better matches in the SciPy fallback. FastSAM box prompts that miss all masks select none, and SAM prompts remain usable after an interrupted “segment everything” call.
- 🖼️ **Utility improvements:** Fixed mask-IoU behavior across data types, backend precision updates after model conversions, ExecuTorch capture issues, binary semantic-mask rendering, and PIL text placement.
- 📚 **Dataset workflow updates:** Argoverse now downloads and converts through Ultralytics Platform instead of Google Drive. Documentation also clarifies how dataset subsets are selected and adds NXP to the listed export options.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- NXP i.MX95 users can compile YOLO models for Neutron hardware using the existing export and inference workflows. Validate accuracy, latency, and CPU fallback on the target board before deployment.
- Safer loading reduces risks from untrusted cache and model files; missing checkpoint dependencies now raise an error rather than being installed automatically.
- The reliability fixes address issues that could cause incorrect matches, unexpected masks, training failures, or plotting errors.
- Faster deterministic semantic-loss computation can reduce training overhead, though the reported speedups are focused measurements rather than guarantees of end-to-end training speed.

## What's Changed

data.name: v8.4.202 - `ultralytics 8.4.202` Save stream prediction videos at the stream's frame rate (#27016)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.202 improves stream-video saving and fixes several compatibility and reliability issues, alongside updated model and benchmark documentation.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🎥 **Stream predictions now save at the stream’s actual frame rate.** RTSP streams, webcams, and `.streams` sources use each stream’s own FPS—including in multi-stream setups—instead of assuming 30 FPS. Video-file and screen capture rates remain unchanged.
- 🔧 **Improved model loading and export compatibility.** MNN exports now expose task metadata before loading, helping renamed pose, segmentation, classification, and OBB models—and RT-DETR exports—be identified correctly. Class-name weight remapping also works when loading CPU checkpoints into GPU models.
- ⚡ **More reliable TensorRT INT8 exports on older GPUs.** Dynamic INT8 builds on GPUs such as the T4 now use a safer minimum input size, avoiding build failures for small inputs.
- 🧰 **Clearer dataset and Platform behavior.** Classification validation now reports a helpful error when neither a `val` nor `test` split exists. Platform training arguments are sent as JSON values rather than being converted to strings.
- 📚 **Updated YOLO27 and benchmark documentation.** YOLO27 results, model details, and FLOPs reporting were corrected; benchmark scores were recalculated to account for ignored regions in VisDrone and HIT-UAV.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ Stream recordings should now play at the right speed, including when streams have different frame rates or frames are skipped.
- ✅ Model loading and deployment workflows are less likely to fail because of metadata, device, or older-GPU INT8 limitations.
- ✅ Dataset setup issues are easier to diagnose, and Platform receives more useful, correctly typed training settings.
- 📖 Updated documentation gives users more accurate performance comparisons and clearer evaluation details. These are documentation corrections, not changes to the models themselves.

data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.201 makes PIL-based plotting up to 15× faster** while keeping visuals consistent, and standardizes the Construction-PPE dataset’s name and download paths. 🚀

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Faster plotting across tasks:** Training and validation mosaics and `Results.plot(pil=True)` benefit from cached fonts and label patches, fewer image conversions, and more efficient mask blending.

The dataset is described as an original Ultralytics dataset, created and open-sourced in November 2026, with 1,000 images, 12 classes, and a CC BY 4.0 license.
- **No model architecture changes** are included in this release.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Quicker visual checks:** Faster plotting can reduce waiting during training, validation, and prediction review, especially when generating many annotated images.
- **Clearer dataset setup:** Consistent naming makes it easier to find and use Construction-PPE. Existing local caches using the old directory name are outside the supported scope of this release.
- **Same plotting appearance:** The optimizations target processing overhead rather than changing how annotations look. ✨

data.name: v8.4.200 - `ultralytics 8.4.200` Display Arabic class names correctly in plots (#27007)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.200 displays Arabic class names correctly in plots and makes training, export, and dataset workflows more reliable.** No model architecture changes are included.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 📝 **Arabic class names display correctly in plots** — Letters now join and read right-to-left in prediction, training and validation images on every install, with numbers and Latin text kept readable. No new dependency or argument is needed. This is the release’s main change.
- 🦺 **Construction-PPE dataset updated** — The new version has 1,000 images, 12 classes, and 14,863 reviewed annotations, with an 800/200 training-validation split. It adds forklift and missing-vest classes and changes class IDs. The new archive is separate from legacy downloads. [Browse the dataset on Ultralytics Platform](https://platform.ultralytics.com/ultralytics/datasets/construction-ppe).
- 🖥️ **Invalid multi-GPU batch sizes fail earlier** — Training now reports an error before distributed training starts if the batch is smaller than the number of GPUs. Batches that are not evenly divisible by the GPU count still work, with the remainder dropped.
- 📦 **Small INT8 calibration datasets are handled more reliably** — When there are fewer calibration images than the requested batch size, images are repeated to fill the batch, helping avoid export failures with some runtimes.
- 📄 **YAML directive headers are accepted** — YAML files with standard `%YAML` or `%TAG` headers can now be parsed instead of being rejected.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Arabic class names in annotated images are now legible on Windows, Linux, macOS and Docker installs where they previously showed as separate, reversed letters.
- The updated Construction-PPE dataset adds coverage for more workplace-safety scenarios, but its changed class ordering may require updates to projects that rely on the old class IDs. The legacy dataset remains available separately.
- Earlier batch-size checks and fuller INT8 calibration batches help users catch training configuration errors sooner and avoid certain export failures.
- YAML files produced by other tools are more likely to work without manual edits.

data.name: v8.4.199 - `ultralytics 8.4.199` Send the raw run name to Ultralytics Platform (#26953)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Ultralytics 8.4.199 improves how training runs appear on Ultralytics Platform, makes several training and profiling workflows more reliable, and clarifies Platform and dataset features in the documentation. **No model architectures changed in this release.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🏷️ **Preserves training run names on Ultralytics Platform:** Local training now sends the original run name, including underscores and non-English characters, instead of stripping those characters before display.
- 🧠 **Improves first-epoch out-of-memory recovery:** When a training run runs out of memory, the retry now reduces the batch size actually used by the data loader. This can help training succeed when the requested batch is larger than the dataset.
- ⚡ **Makes TensorRT profiling more consistent:** Profiling rebuilds the TensorRT engine for each run and rounds image size to the model’s stride, helping ensure benchmark results reflect the requested settings.
- 📊 **Corrects single-class segmentation plots:** Pixel counts in `labels.jpg` now show the foreground class rather than the background for single-class semantic datasets.
- 📚 **Documents additional workflows and features:** Dataset splits can now be described as accepting individual image files as well as directories and image lists. The docs also explain how to share a public model’s Predict tab, and cover public comments and ONNX INT8 quantization updates.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 📝 Run names are easier to recognize and match with local experiments, especially when they include underscores or non-ASCII characters.
- 🔄 OOM retries are more likely to make progress on small datasets or when the requested batch exceeds the data loader’s actual batch.
- 🔍 TensorRT benchmark results are less likely to rely on an outdated engine or a mismatched image size.
- ✅ Single-class segmentation charts provide more useful class statistics, making dataset checks clearer.
- 🌐 Users can find clearer guidance for sharing models, configuring datasets, and applying ONNX quantization.

data.name: v8.4.198 - `ultralytics 8.4.198` Save NumPy float64 values as numbers in YAML files (#26993)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.198 makes training settings and YAML files more reliable, alongside fixes to downloads, dataset errors, and documentation.** No model architecture or pretrained-weight changes are included.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **NumPy learning rates now save correctly in YAML** — The main change converts `np.float64` values to ordinary numeric values when writing YAML. Training arguments such as sweep-generated learning rates can now be saved and reused from `args.yaml`.
- **More robust YAML parsing** — Fixes handling of block-scalar indentation, whitespace-only lines, and nodes written on their own lines, bringing the built-in parser closer to YAML conventions.
- **Improved download and dataset errors** — Downloads now identify themselves with an Ultralytics User-Agent, helping avoid some servers rejecting requests. Missing classification datasets now produce a clear file-not-found error instead of a confusing failed-download message.
- **More dependable training and logging** — Updates the minimum supported versions of `ultralytics-thop` and `ultralytics-platform`; also suppresses a Triton warning that could appear during profiling.
- **Clearer documentation** — Explains how relative `project` paths are resolved and standardizes how metrics such as mAP and depth accuracy are written across docs and benchmark tables.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🔁 **Reuse training configurations more easily:** NumPy-based hyperparameter sweeps no longer produce YAML values that reload as strings and fail validation.
- 🧰 **Fewer confusing failures:** YAML parsing, downloads, and missing-dataset handling are more predictable.
- 📚 **Easier to follow guidance and compare results:** Consistent metric labels and clarified path behavior reduce ambiguity.
- ✅ **No model migration needed:** These updates improve tooling and documentation rather than changing model behavior.

## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.197 makes AMP checks work without downloading model weights and removes PyYAML from the base dependencies.** 🚀

## 📊 Key Changes
- **AMP checks no longer download a checkpoint.** The check builds an untrained YOLO26n from its YAML config and compares FP32 and AMP results across convolution and attention layers.

- 📦 **Simpler installation:** Removing PyYAML from the base requirements reduces a dependency for standard installs. The built-in parser covers Ultralytics’ common YAML needs, but it is not intended to support every YAML feature.
- 📄 **More consistent YAML handling:** Users can use the same built-in utility to load and save supported Ultralytics YAML files.

data.name: v8.4.196 - `ultralytics 8.4.196` Improve ONNX INT8 accuracy with per-channel weight quantization (#26978)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Release **v8.4.196** improves ONNX INT8 model accuracy and makes several practical fixes to training, video analytics, exports, and documentation.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **More accurate ONNX INT8 exports:** The main update applies per-channel weight quantization for ONNX opset 13 and newer, helping preserve smaller weight values that can be lost with a single scale. Older opsets retain per-tensor quantization. On the reported COCO evaluation, detection mAP rose from **0.3557 to 0.3814**, while segmentation box mAP rose from **0.3213 to 0.3595** and mask mAP from **0.2862 to 0.3046**. Some classes may still score lower. The change was tested with all 167 existing ONNX tests passing, and 51 INT8 artifacts loading and running on ONNX Runtime 1.20.0. [See PR #26978](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26978).
- **More reliable video solutions:** Speed estimation now uses the source video’s frame rate by default, while an explicitly set FPS still takes precedence. Analytics output also uses the chart’s actual dimensions, avoiding empty output videos in some configurations.
- **Safer training and data handling:** Resume now selects the checkpoint most recently modified, including on Windows. DOTA readers and annotation visualization now accept UTF-8 BOM label files, and semantic training preserves small positive class-weight totals when normalizing cross-entropy loss.
- **Cleaner model exports:** Re-exporting to RKNN, Ascend, ExecuTorch, or IMX replaces old files in the output directory, reducing the risk of accidentally loading a stale model.
- **Updated guidance:** The screen-prediction example now uses streaming, so it can handle a continuous source without collecting results indefinitely. DGX Spark guidance now recommends TensorRT FP16 over INT8 for YOLO26 at batch size 1, based on measurements showing INT8 was slower for smaller models and less accurate across the tested models. Documentation links, wording, and several technical details were also corrected.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 📈 **Better quality from quantized ONNX models:** Per-channel scales can reduce accuracy loss in INT8 exports, including the near-constant depth-map issue reported for YOLO26 depth exports.
- ⚙️ **More dependable workflows:** Checkpoint selection, DOTA label reading, video analytics, and model re-exports behave more predictably in common edge cases.
- 🧭 **Clearer usage and deployment advice:** Updated examples and hardware-specific precision recommendations help users avoid misleading results and choose a suitable export option.

## What's Changed
* Polish wording on SAM 3, Solutions, Sony IMX500, Kaggle, IBM watsonx and FastSAM docs by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26980
* Weave reference links into docs prose and correct dataset, model and integration details by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26981
* Select the most recently saved checkpoint when resuming by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26973
* Accept UTF-8 BOM labels in DOTA splitting and annotation visualization by @Sonica-B in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26882

* Preserve weighted semantic cross-entropy normalization by @aswanth-07 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26969
* Fix the screen and webcam examples that never return by @Echoslayer in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26979
* Replace the RKNN, Ascend, ExecuTorch and IMX export directories on re-export by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26941

## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.195 adds early Python 3.15 compatibility checks, fixes AutoBatch profiling on older PyTorch versions, and improves documentation accuracy across hundreds of pages.**

## 📊 Key Changes

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ Gives maintainers an early way to catch compatibility issues as Python 3.15 support becomes available, while clearly limiting tests that depend on packages without compatible wheels.
- 🚀 Makes AutoBatch profiling more reliable for users running older PyTorch versions and helps restore affected Jetson tests.
- 🔎 Makes documentation easier to trust and navigate, with clearer dataset guidance and more accurate examples.
- ℹ️ **No major model or architecture changes** are included in this release.

data.name: v8.4.194 - `ultralytics 8.4.194` Size AutoBatch from the train dataset for every task (#26956)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Ultralytics **8.4.194** makes automatic batch sizing more reliable across tasks, alongside practical fixes for model loading, results saving, datasets, and deployment workflows.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🚀 **Automatic batch sizing now uses the training dataset for every task.** It accounts for dataset size and labels across classification, detection, and multi-dataset training. If profiling runs out of memory during backward computation, AutoBatch treats that as a limit rather than relying on an invalid measurement.
- 🛡️ **Model YAML parsing is safer and more consistent.** Activations must resolve to supported `torch.nn` modules, and model entries must be PyTorch module classes. Custom YAMLs using other expressions may need updating.
- 💾 **Saving prediction results is more robust.** `Results.save()` and `plot(save=True)` now produce sensible `.jpg` filenames for sources such as webcams, videos, or missing paths, and create parent directories when needed.
- 🔄 **Similarity search uses the selected image directory on each startup.** This avoids reusing stale indexes from another dataset; the trade-off is that embeddings are rebuilt each time.
- 🧩 **Dataset and URL handling is more dependable.** Non-PNG semantic masks are resolved before cache hashing, and URL schemes such as `HTTPS://`, `GS://`, and `UL://` are now handled without case sensitivity.
- 📈 **Benchmarking and evaluation guidance are clearer.** TensorFlow GraphDef benchmarks now include OBB and pose, and the docs explain that classes absent from validation receive the overall mAP value rather than a measured per-class score.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ AutoBatch is less likely to choose a batch size that exceeds a small dataset or available GPU memory, and multi-dataset World/YOLOE training avoids label-access failures.
- 🔒 Consistent, restricted YAML parsing improves safety, though nonstandard custom model configurations may no longer load.
- 🧰 More reliable result saving, mask-cache updates, and URL routing reduce common workflow errors.
- 🔍 Similarity search results better reflect the images currently in the chosen folder, while requiring index-building work at startup.
- 📚 Documentation updates clarify metric interpretation and integration behavior; no new model architecture is introduced in this release.

data.name: v8.4.193 - `ultralytics 8.4.193` Up to 2x faster CPU ONNX Runtime and OpenVINO prediction (#26942)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.193 makes CPU inference with ONNX Runtime and OpenVINO substantially faster on some systems, alongside fixes that improve export behavior, data handling, training reliability, and documentation.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🚀 **Faster CPU inference — the main release change:** For CPU ONNX Runtime and OpenVINO models, PyTorch now uses at most two threads for preprocessing and postprocessing, reducing competition with the inference runtime. On an 8-vCPU test machine, prediction was **19–54% faster** across the tested backends and batch sizes. On 4 vCPUs, results were mostly unchanged, with one ONNX Runtime batch test slightly slower. PyTorch `.pt` setup is unchanged.
- 📐 **Dynamic exports use their intended image size:** When a dynamic export is loaded without an explicit `imgsz`, prediction and validation now default to the size recorded in the export metadata. This avoids silently running models at an unsuitable default resolution; an explicitly provided size still takes precedence.
- 🧰 **More dependable data and visualization workflows:** Dataset loading now accepts individual image paths. Related fixes improve annotated-image splitting with relative paths, replace stale auto-annotation labels with empty files when no objects are found, clip DOTA tile labels instead of discarding affected tiles, prevent perspective augmentation from creating huge ghost boxes, and avoid altering shared image batches while plotting.
- ✅ **Improved model and metric correctness:** Class names are returned in class-ID order; semantic metrics handle compact `uint8` labels correctly; and W&B class curves now skip label-less validation splits and use the right class names. YOLOE now clearly rejects visual prompts on fused models rather than failing later or reporting misleading results.
- 🏋️ **Training and checkpoint fixes:** AutoBatch profiling better reflects the actual training loss for RT-DETR and semantic segmentation. Distillation checkpoints saved mid-run can load their student model, while resumed distillation training retains its wrapper state.
- 📦 **Smoother exports and installs:** Exported model paths and ONNX Runtime variants receive more consistent handling, and automatic dependency installation now prefers `uv` when available—including on ARM64. The release also updates CI coverage for newer PyTorch versions on Python 3.14.
- 📚 **Documentation and Platform updates:** Export guides clarify format behavior and limitations, including the transition from TF.js export to LiteRT. Platform docs also cover eligible Enterprise HIPAA BAAs, early-access annotation, and bulk deletion controls.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ⚡ **CPU deployment users may see a major inference speedup**, particularly on 8-vCPU systems using ONNX Runtime or OpenVINO. The change is limited to those CPU backends and does not alter `.pt` setup.
- 🎯 **Exported models are more likely to run at the resolution they were designed for**, helping avoid unexpected prediction or validation results when `imgsz` is omitted.
- 🛠️ **Training and dataset workflows are more robust:** fewer silently skipped images or tiles, less stale annotation output, and more trustworthy metrics and plots.
- 🔎 **Results and errors are clearer:** class labels stay aligned with class IDs, and unsupported YOLOE visual-prompt workflows now fail with a direct explanation.
- 📝 **Documentation better reflects current behavior**, helping users choose export settings and understand Platform features.

data.name: v8.4.192 - Support torch 2.15 CUDA in DDP training and ONNX Runtime inference (#26928)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
v8.4.192 improves compatibility with PyTorch 2.15 and CUDA 13 for multi-GPU training and ONNX Runtime GPU inference, alongside a small update to Platform response documentation.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **More reliable multi-GPU training:** On PyTorch 2.8 and newer, each NCCL process group is explicitly bound to the GPU selected for its training rank. This helps prevent device-mismatch errors, especially when GPUs are selected in a non-default order.
- **More dependable ONNX GPU inference:** Linux CUDA setups now install ONNX Runtime’s CUDA dependencies and preload their libraries, helping prevent a missing cuRAND library from causing inference to fall back to the CPU.
- **Updated CUDA tooling:** The Docker training image now uses PyTorch 2.15, and the export image and GPU CI setup include the required ONNX Runtime CUDA package.
- **Clearer Platform API docs:** Prediction response examples no longer list `metadata.classNames`. Class names remain available on individual detections; dataset and model class names are unchanged.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🖥️ **Fewer multi-GPU training failures** for setups that use GPUs in a custom order or select GPUs dynamically.
- ⚡ **More reliable GPU acceleration for ONNX Runtime** on supported Linux CUDA environments, reducing unintended CPU fallback.
- 🧰 **Better alignment across development, CI, and Docker environments** when using newer PyTorch and CUDA dependencies.
- 📦 **Slightly leaner, more accurate API examples** that match the Platform prediction response.

No model architecture or prediction behavior changes are indicated in this release.

## What's Changed

data.name: v8.4.191 - `ultralytics 8.4.191` Fix RKNN INT8 accuracy with a host-side decode tail for all tasks (#26904)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Release **v8.4.191** improves RKNN INT8 exports, especially for tasks beyond detection, and includes performance and tracking fixes plus Platform documentation updates.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **RKNN INT8 export — main update:** INT8 export is now enabled for detection, segmentation, pose, and oriented bounding box (OBB) models. The NPU runs the head’s output convolutions, while a new `tail.onnx` file runs the box decoding on the CPU in floating point. FP16-capable targets also use RKNN’s `auto_hybrid` option to retain high-error layers in floating point.
- **RKNN deployment notes:** The decode tail requires ONNX Runtime, which Ultralytics installs automatically when needed. Custom runtimes must run `tail.onnx` or implement the same decoding. Re-export INT8 models made with earlier versions to avoid incorrect coordinate scaling. INT8 accuracy has been tested in the RKNN simulator, but not yet validated on Rockchip hardware.
- **Faster segmentation training:** Finds foreground anchors across the batch in one pass instead of repeating work per image. Losses and gradients remain unchanged; the reported Tesla T4 timings show modest training-step improvements.
- **More efficient parking management:** Computes each tracked car’s center once per frame rather than once for every parking-space comparison, reducing repeated work.
- **Improved OC-SORT matching:** Measures detection direction over the track’s recent `delta_t`-frame window, making associations less sensitive to box jitter.
- **Preserved prediction-manifest order:** Images and videos listed in TXT or CSV sources are now processed in the order provided, rather than being reordered alphabetically.
- **Platform and guide updates:** Platform documentation now includes MiniMax as an annotation provider, explains saved Roboflow and W&B import keys and OBB labels in detection datasets, and features an updated YOLO26 batch-processing video.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- The RKNN change targets the accuracy loss caused by running box decoding in INT8 on the NPU. Keeping that decode on the CPU in floating point is intended to improve accuracy and broaden INT8 support across vision tasks.
- The training and parking-management changes reduce unnecessary repeated work without changing the described outputs, while the OC-SORT fix may help maintain more reliable tracking when detections are jittery.
- Manifest ordering now better matches the sequence users explicitly specify—useful, for example, when listing video frames in playback order.

## What's Changed
* Platform docs: add MiniMax to the paid annotation vendors by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26902
* Find segment loss foreground anchors once per batch by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26914

data.name: v8.4.190 - `ultralytics 8.4.190` Mask-IoU-aware label assignment for YOLO26-seg (#26773)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
YOLO 8.4.190 improves YOLO26 segmentation training by making label assignment consider mask quality as well as box overlap, alongside fixes for model export, inference, training utilities, and data handling.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🎭 **YOLO26-seg mask-aware training:** Positive training matches now account for both box and mask overlap. The implementation limits mask decoding and uses safer precision to control memory use and avoid numerical overflow. Other segmentation models and inference/export behavior are unchanged.
- 📱 **More reliable CoreML support:** Fixes address duplicate detections in segmentation exports, floating-point output crashes on MPS, and unnecessary NumPy downgrades during inference. Oriented-box NMS also receives a precision fix.
- 🧠 **RKNN depth INT8 export:** Depth models can now be exported in INT8, with hybrid precision to keep error-prone layers in FP16. Calibration should use paired depth maps covering the deployment scene’s depth range.
- ⚡ **Inference and training improvements:** OpenVINO CPU inference can load upcoming batches while the current batch runs. AutoBatch better accounts for GPU memory available to the process when selecting a batch size.
- 🗂️ **Data and usability fixes:** NDJSON conversion skips unlabeled classification images instead of treating them as class 0. FastSAM handles text prompts when no masks qualify, and region-drawing solutions accept floating-point coordinates.
- 🚀 **Faster segmentation validation:** COCO mask RLE encoding is vectorized, reducing encoding time in tested workloads.
- 📚 **Documentation and tooling:** Platform docs clarify dataset and project cloning options, mobile export links, and annotation model comparisons. The CPU runner also includes English Tesseract data for scanned-PDF workflows.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- YOLO26 segmentation training can make assignments that better reflect mask quality, while keeping mask-specific work bounded in computation and memory.
- Users exporting or running models on Apple and Rockchip hardware should encounter fewer precision-related issues and gain support for depth-model INT8 export on RKNN.
- Better batch sizing and CPU prefetching may improve GPU utilization and OpenVINO CPU throughput, while the data and prompting fixes prevent common failures or misleading labels.

data.name: v8.4.189 - `ultralytics 8.4.189` Fix IMX requirements, Hailo seg end nodes and unreadable-dataset errors (#26883)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.189 improves deployment reliability and inference robustness**, with key fixes for Sony IMX500 and Hailo exports, clearer dataset errors, and safer handling of model outputs. No model architecture changes were introduced.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **More reliable IMX500 exports:** Updated converter requirements and aligned dependency versions. IMX500 export is now explicitly supported on Linux with Python 3.10–3.12.
- **Fixed Hailo segmentation exports:** The segmentation prototype output node is now detected from the exported model, helping accommodate different model activations.
- **Clearer dataset failures:** Unreadable datasets are less likely to be reported misleadingly as datasets with no labels.
- **Broader export compatibility:** Replaced several `einsum` operations with equivalent matrix multiplications, enabling affected YOLOE and YOLO-World models to export to ONNX at lower opsets.
- **More robust predictions and results:** Classification probabilities are preserved between inference calls; grayscale images and results without boxes are handled more safely.
- **Safer TensorFlow exports:** Existing ONNX Runtime variants, including Windows ML and Vitis AI builds, are recognized to avoid unnecessary runtime replacement.
- **Updated mobile guidance and benchmarks:** LiteRT, QNN, and Core ML performance tables were refreshed, and Platform documentation now explains how to open compatible exports in the Ultralytics YOLO app.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Fewer deployment and setup failures:** The IMX500 dependency and Python-version updates address real export and inference issues; Hailo and ONNX fixes broaden export compatibility.
- **More dependable inference:** Saved classification results no longer change when a backend reuses its output buffer, and image/result utilities better handle uncommon inputs.
- **Easier troubleshooting:** Dataset errors are less confusing, helping users identify the underlying issue sooner.
- **Better mobile deployment guidance:** Updated device measurements and app instructions make it easier to evaluate and try exported models on phones.

data.name: v8.4.188 - ultralytics 8.4.188 Fix Android loading and depth speed of QNN exports (#26872)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Release **8.4.188** improves QNN exports for Android, removes an unnecessary operation from non-LiteRT depth exports, and updates the LiteRT export toolchain.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Fixes Android QNN model loading:** QNN exports now keep input and output quantization inside the QNN context. This avoids an `io_name_overrides` attribute that newer QNN export tools can add but Android’s built-in QNN Execution Provider cannot read.
- **Speeds up depth exports outside LiteRT:** The export-only ReLU is now applied only for LiteRT. It remains there as a workaround for an Intel NPU compiler issue, but is avoided in QNN and other formats.
- **Updates LiteRT export requirements:** Minimum versions are raised to `litert-torch 0.10.0`, `ai-edge-litert 2.3.0`, and `ai-edge-quantizer 0.10.0`.
- **Refreshes the export Docker image:** It now installs the full export dependency set, including LiteRT support.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 📱 **Android users** should be able to load affected QNN exports with ONNX Runtime’s built-in QNN provider, including in apps using the Ultralytics Flutter plugin.
- ⚡ **Depth-model exports** may run more efficiently where the ReLU workaround is not needed.
- 📦 **LiteRT exporters** use a newer toolchain aligned with current mobile NPU runtimes, which can improve compatibility when exporting for supported devices.
- 🧩 These are export and deployment improvements; the release does not change model architecture or weights.

## What's Changed

data.name: v8.4.187 - ultralytics 8.4.187 OKS-only label assignment with a pyramid-level gate for YOLO26-pose (#26843)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
YOLO26-pose training now assigns keypoints using pose accuracy, with a feature-pyramid scale gate to help match objects to suitable training anchors.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **OKS-only matching:** For ground truths with visible keypoints, assignment now uses keypoint similarity (OKS) instead of blending it with box overlap.
- **Scale-aware candidate selection:** An FCOS-style gate limits candidate anchors to pyramid levels suited to each object’s size. The finest and coarsest levels remain available for objects outside the usual size range.
- **Fallbacks preserved:** If the gate would leave a ground truth with no candidates, the ungated candidates are retained. Ground truths without visible keypoints continue to use box overlap.
- **Training-only scope:** The change applies to YOLO26-pose training by default. It adds no configuration options or dependencies and does not change inference, export, or the model architecture.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🎯 Encourages training assignments to favor anchors with more accurate keypoints.
- 📏 Helps pure keypoint-based matching account for object size across feature-pyramid levels.
- 🛠️ Users get the updated behavior automatically when training YOLO26-pose; no migration steps are needed.

data.name: v8.4.185 - Load MNN on glibc 2.41+ by clearing its unused executable-stack flag (#26861)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
This release primarily fixes MNN loading on newer Linux systems, while improving ONNX deployment options, export reliability, and several training and inference workflows.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **MNN on newer Linux:** The headline change addresses an import failure on glibc 2.41+ systems, including Ubuntu 25.04/26.04 and Debian 13. Ultralytics now clears an unused executable-stack flag in affected MNN x86_64 modules before importing them, allowing MNN export and inference to work.
- **More ONNX deployment choices:** On supported Windows 11 systems, users can explicitly install Windows ML’s ONNX Runtime and let it select hardware execution providers. Existing session options are preserved.
- **Improved Edge TPU exports on Python 3.13:** TensorFlow export now uses a compatible `onnx2tf` 1.x version across Python versions. In reported testing, this changed a YOLO26 export from 20 to 652 operations mapped to the Edge TPU, with far fewer left for the CPU.
- **Training and inference fixes:** Classification resume now retains the checkpoint’s image size. LLM image input handles 16-bit PIL and NumPy images more consistently, and failed training runs clean up experiment-tracking runs and Platform console capture.
- **Other reliability and performance improvements:** HSV augmentation now uses a single multi-channel lookup operation; large confusion-matrix plots retain the background row and column; and Google Drive downloads better support direct links and uppercase URLs.
- **Platform and documentation updates:** Docs now cover importing W&B checkpoints and clarify cloud-storage AI features, image-generation permissions, Roboflow imports, and browser-side image resizing. Citation blocks are also presented consistently across documentation.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Unblocks MNN users on modern Linux:** The executable-stack flag was not needed by MNN’s kernels, but newer glibc versions reject it. Clearing it should restore MNN imports without changing MNN’s actual inference behavior.
- **Expands hardware deployment options:** Windows ML provides an opt-in route for ONNX inference on supported Windows devices, while the `onnx2tf` adjustment helps more exported model operations run on Edge TPU rather than falling back to CPU.
- **Makes workflows more dependable:** Resuming classification training, passing image data to LLMs, downloading Google Drive files, and handling training failures should now behave more consistently.
- **Makes Platform capabilities and requirements easier to understand:** The documentation clarifies how to connect and use integrations, including when cloud-storage write access is needed.

## 🌟 Summary
A reliability-focused release with an important TIFF-reading fix, plus improvements to segmentation prompts, model loading, validation, integrations, and Platform workflows—without introducing a new model architecture.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Multi-page TIFF handling (PR #26842):** By default, grayscale TIFF scans now load as their first page instead of incorrectly combining pages into image channels. Only `cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED` stacks same-size pages, preserving the option for multispectral workflows.
- **More reliable YOLOE and YOLO-World loading:** Checkpoint type now determines the correct model wrapper, so specialized models continue to work when saved under generic filenames such as `best.pt`. Changing class names on a text-fused YOLOE model now raises a clear error instead of silently relabeling predictions or failing later.
- **More faithful SAM mask refinement:** Floating-point prompt masks retain negative and fractional values, avoiding unintended changes to mask-refinement inputs.
- **Improved data and metric handling:** Fixes cover multipart polygon connections, confusion-matrix matching, classification prediction with rectangular image sizes, and validation on datasets without labels. Dataset downloads also recognize archive URLs with query strings.
- **Smoother integrations and runtime behavior:** Weights & Biases now supports training inside a user-started run, preserving its settings and leaving it open afterward. Additional fixes improve Platform training resume behavior and OpenVINO/LiteRT device handling.
- **Updated CI and documentation:** CPU runners gain SSH, `rsync`, and libraries needed to import GUI OpenCV. Documentation clarifies Platform dataset workflows and training features, corrects export examples, and refreshes several guides and screenshots.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Prevents TIFF-related training failures:** Scanned documents are no longer mistaken for multi-channel images or allowed to produce images with excessive channel counts. Users who intentionally need TIFF pages as bands should use `cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED`.
- **Makes model and data workflows more predictable:** Correct model selection, clearer YOLOE class-change errors, and more accurate mask and polygon handling reduce confusing failures and incorrect results.
- **Improves validation and experiment tracking:** Label-free validation avoids unnecessary warnings, confusion-matrix matching is more consistent, and existing W&B runs retain their history and remain available for further logging.

data.name: v8.4.183 - ultralytics 8.4.183 Update Axelera SDK to 1.9.0 and support every YOLO26 task (#26788)
data.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.183 expands hardware deployment and improves reliability across training, prediction, data handling, and evaluation.** 🚀

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Axelera Metis support for every YOLO26 task:** With Voyager SDK 1.9.0, detection, instance and semantic segmentation, depth estimation, pose, OBB, and classification models can all export, predict, and validate through `yolo`. The NMS-free detection path is used by default. SDK 1.8 exports remain compatible; the updated setup requires `metis-dkms` 1.7.0 or newer and supports PyTorch versions below 2.15.
- **Higher Axelera throughput:** In the documented COCO128 benchmark, SDK 1.9 reached **109 images per second at batch 32**, compared with 40 images per second on SDK 1.8. Larger prediction batches can improve throughput; batch size 1 remains useful when per-image latency matters.
- **Intel acceleration for LiteRT models:** LiteRT exports can now run on Intel CPUs and NPUs, including support for YOLO26 task types such as detection, segmentation, depth, pose, OBB, and classification.
- **More reliable training and depth calibration:** Fixes address warmup and gradient accumulation edge cases, MPS memory growth during training, and depth calibration replacing an already-good calibration with a worse one. Interrupted runs can also resume under the same Ultralytics Platform model, and W&B resuming works on Windows.
- **More accurate and robust data workflows:** Fixes improve ImageNet-subset classifier validation, accept UTF-8 labels with a byte-order mark, preserve non-ASCII grounding annotations, convert COCO RLE masks for segmentation, and align 16-bit NumPy images with image-file prediction behavior.
- **Prediction, export, and visualization fixes:** Negative FastSAM points now reliably exclude masks regardless of prompt order. Other fixes cover very thin images, rectangular INT8 calibration, grayscale LiteRT models, semantic overlay colors, depth-map saving, and several additional edge cases.
- **Platform and documentation updates:** Platform documentation now includes Gemma 4 and Nemotron as hosted annotation models and explains new visibility controls and workflows. Benchmark instructions were also clarified for NMS-free evaluation.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Deploy YOLO26 on more hardware and tasks:** Axelera users can use one integrated workflow across all seven YOLO26 tasks, while Intel LiteRT users gain CPU and NPU inference options.
- **Get better throughput when processing batches:** Axelera SDK 1.9 can substantially increase prediction throughput for larger batches, though actual results depend on hardware and workload.
- **Trust training, validation, and predictions more:** The fixes reduce avoidable failures and make reported results better reflect the supplied data and model—for example, correcting classifier label alignment changes ImageNette validation accuracy from **9.45% to 70.37%** in the reported test.
- **Keep existing workflows working:** Many changes are targeted bug fixes or compatibility improvements; notably, Axelera models exported with SDK 1.8 do not need to be re-exported for SDK 1.9.

## 🌟 Summary
YOLO 8.4.182 strengthens dataset label checks to catch invalid bounding boxes before they break validation plotting, and improves Linux drive reporting.
